# Review pack: Yunus and the fish

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/yunus-and-the-fish.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the mission of Yunus, the fish and the people he was sent to. None is used in this draft.
- The later chapter speaks of the man of the fish and of the one with the fish without naming Yunus; the link rests on the epithet and the matching events, as in the event inventory. A scholar should confirm.
- The verb abaqa (37:140) is rendered 'went away' and is often rendered 'fled'. The Arabic naqdira (21:87) is rendered 'constrain'; it is read as having power over him by others. The words for blameworthy (muliim, madhmum) are rendered plainly.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The ship and the fish  (`#the-ship-and-the-fish`)

Cited ayat: 37:139-148

> **37:139** وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
>
> **37:140** إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
>
> **37:141** فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ
>
> **37:142** فَٱلْتَقَمَهُ ٱلْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ
>
> **37:143** فَلَوْلَآ أَنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَبِّحِينَ
>
> **37:144** لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
>
> **37:145** فَنَبَذْنَٰهُ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ
>
> **37:146** وَأَنۢبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِّن يَقْطِينٍ
>
> **37:147** وَأَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ
>
> **37:148** فَـَٔامَنُوا۟ فَمَتَّعْنَٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

### Claims

**c1** (37:139): Yunus was among the messengers.

**c2** (37:140): He went away to the laden ship.

**c3** (37:141): He cast lots and was among those who lost.

**c4** (37:142): The fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy.

**c5** (37:143-144): Had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly until the day they are raised.

**c6** (37:145): God cast him on the open ground, and he was sick.

**c7** (37:146): God caused a tree of yaqtin to grow over him.

**c8** (37:147-148): God sent him to a hundred thousand or more; they believed, and God let them enjoy life for a time.

### One-minute summary

Yunus, one of the messengers, went away to the laden ship, and the fish swallowed him [c1][c2][c4]. God cast him on the open ground, sent him to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed [c6][c8].

### Complete story

The ayat say that Yunus was among the messengers [c1]. He went away to the laden ship, cast lots and was among those who lost [c2][c3].

The fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy [c4]. Had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly until the day they are raised [c5].

God cast him on the open ground, and he was sick, and caused a tree of yaqtin to grow over him [c6][c7]. God sent him to a hundred thousand or more; they believed, and God let them enjoy life for a time [c8].

### Deep study

The ayat give the cause of his rescue as his glorifying of God, and say what would otherwise have happened [c5]. The word for blameworthy describes him at the moment the fish swallowed him [c4]. The mission is told after the rescue: the number is given as a hundred thousand or more, and the result is that they believed [c8].

### Kids mode

Yunus was one of God's messengers, and he went away on a ship that was full [c1][c2]. A fish swallowed him, but he glorified God, and God cast him out on open ground and made a tree grow over him [c4][c5][c6][c7]. Then God sent him to a hundred thousand people or more, and they believed [c8].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tie his rescue to his glorifying of God [c5]. Another is that the account ends with a whole people who believed and were allowed to enjoy life for a time [c8].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: why he went away, where he was sent first, where the ship sailed, or what the lots decided; the verses say only that he went away to the laden ship and cast lots.
- Not established: how long he stayed in the fish, where he was cast out, or what kind of tree the yaqtin was.
- Not established: the name of the people he was sent to, the place, or how long they were allowed to enjoy life.
- Not established: whether the sending to a hundred thousand or more happened before or after the events at sea; the verses tell it afterwards.

## 2. The call in the darkness  (`#the-call-in-the-darkness`)

Cited ayat: 21:87-88, 68:48-50

> **21:87** وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
>
> **21:88** فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُـۨجِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

> **68:48** فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ
>
> **68:49** لَّوْلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ
>
> **68:50** فَٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَجَعَلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (21:87): The man of the fish went away angry, thought that We would not constrain him, and called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers.

**c2** (21:88): God answered him and saved him from distress, and said that He saves the believers in this way.

**c3** (68:48): The hearer is told to be patient with the judgement of his Lord and not to be like the man of the fish when he cried out while choked with grief.

**c4** (68:49): Had a favour from his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast on the open ground while blameworthy.

**c5** (68:50): His Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.

### One-minute summary

The man of the fish went away angry, and called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. God answered him and saved him from distress, chose him and made him among the righteous [c2][c5].

### Complete story

The man of the fish went away angry, thought that We would not constrain him, and called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. God answered him and saved him from distress, and said that He saves the believers in this way [c2].

Another passage tells the hearer to be patient with the judgement of his Lord and not to be like the man of the fish when he cried out while choked with grief [c3]. It says that, had a favour from his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast on the open ground while blameworthy [c4]. His Lord chose him and made him among the righteous [c5].

### Deep study

The cry has its parts in the ayah: that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. The Arabic for constrain can also be read as having power over him, and the draft keeps it open [c1]. The ayat give God's answer as an answer to the cry and say the same is done for the believers [c2].

### Kids mode

The man of the fish called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. God answered him and saved him from his distress [c2]. God chose him and made him among the righteous [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat teach a prayer of praise and admission, and say that God answered it [c1][c2]. Another is that the hearer is told to be patient and not to be like him in his grief [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: that the man of the fish is the messenger named in the other chapter is read from the epithet and the matching events; the ayat here do not name him.
- Not established: what the darkness was, or where he was when he called; the Arabic word is plural and is not explained in the verses.
- Not established: what he was angry about, or what he thought of being constrained; the Arabic verb allows more than one rendering.
- Not established: how long the distress lasted.
